notes.summary: Geography gives about 2 to 4 questions per paper. Indian geography is asked far more than world geography. The top areas in past papers are rivers and dams, Census 2011 figures, passes and peaks, the monsoon and local winds, soils and crops, and mineral states. Learn rivers with their source and the dams on them, and the Census toppers and bottom states.

concepts.title: Solar system
concepts.body:
PlanetRemember for
MercuryNearest to the Sun, smallest planet, no moon
VenusHottest and brightest planet; spins east to west; called Earth's twin; morning and evening star
EarthOnly known planet with life; 'blue planet'
MarsRed planet (iron oxide); moons Phobos and Deimos; Olympus Mons
JupiterLargest planet; Great Red Spot; Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system
SaturnBright rings; least dense; largest moon Titan
UranusRolls on its side (large tilt); spins east to west
NeptuneFarthest planet
  • Pluto was made a dwarf planet in 2006.
  • The Sun is mostly hydrogen (about three-quarters) and helium. Sunlight takes about 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach the Earth.
  • Brightest star in the night sky: Sirius (Dog Star). Nearest star after the Sun: Proxima Centauri. Pole Star: Polaris.
  • The Earth is about 4.5 billion years old.

concepts.title: Earth's motions, latitudes and time
concepts.body:
• Rotation (west to east, about 24 hours) gives day and night. Revolution (about 365¼ days) with the tilted axis (23½°) gives seasons.
  • Summer solstice: 21 June (longest day in the northern hemisphere). Winter solstice: 22 December. Equinoxes (equal day and night): 21 March and 23 September.
  • Perihelion (nearest the Sun): about 3 January. Aphelion (farthest): about 4 July.
  • Key latitudes: Equator 0°, Tropic of Cancer 23½°N, Tropic of Capricorn 23½°S, Arctic Circle 66½°N, Antarctic Circle 66½°S.
  • Longitude: 360° = 24 hours, so 15° = 1 hour and 1° = 4 minutes. Prime Meridian: 0° (Greenwich). International Date Line: about 180°.
  • Indian Standard Time uses 82°30′E (passing near Mirzapur, UP). IST = GMT + 5 hours 30 minutes.

concepts.title: Earth's interior, rocks and landforms
concepts.body:
• Layers: crust (silica and alumina, 'sial'), mantle, core (nickel and iron, 'nife'). Mohorovičić (Moho) discontinuity separates crust and mantle; Gutenberg discontinuity separates mantle and core.
  • Earthquakes: the point inside is the focus (hypocentre); the point above it on the surface is the epicentre. Measured on the Richter scale with a seismograph. P waves are fastest; S waves cannot pass through liquid; surface (L) waves do the most damage.
  • Continental drift: Alfred Wegener (1912), one supercontinent Pangaea surrounded by Panthalassa. Sea-floor spreading: Harry Hess, 'History of Ocean Basins' (1962). Both led to plate tectonics.
  • Volcanoes: most lie on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire'. India's only active volcano is Barren Island (Andaman Sea).
Rock typeHow it formsExamples
Igneous (primary)Cooling of magma or lavaGranite, basalt
SedimentaryLayers of deposits; may hold fossilsSandstone, limestone, shale, coal
MetamorphicChanged by heat and pressureMarble (from limestone), slate (from shale), quartzite (from sandstone), gneiss (from granite)

Petrology is the study of rocks. Landforms: fold mountains (Himalayas, Alps, Andes, Rockies); block mountains and rift valleys (Narmada valley); river features (V-shaped valley, gorge, meander, ox-bow lake, delta); glacial (U-shaped valley, cirque, moraine); wind (sand dunes, barchans, mushroom rocks); limestone caves (stalactites hang down, stalagmites rise up).

concepts.title: Atmosphere and winds
concepts.body:
Air: nitrogen 78%, oxygen 21%, argon about 0.93%, carbon dioxide about 0.04%.

LayerFeature
TroposphereLowest; all weather; temperature falls with height
StratosphereOzone layer; good for jet planes
MesosphereColdest layer; meteors burn up
Thermosphere (ionosphere)Reflects radio waves; auroras
ExosphereOutermost
  • Planetary winds: trade winds (towards the equator), westerlies (mid-latitudes), polar easterlies. The Coriolis force turns winds to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern.
  • Cyclone names: hurricanes (Atlantic), typhoons (western Pacific and China Sea), willy-willies (Australia), tropical cyclones (Indian Ocean). A waterspout is a rotating column of air over water, usually weaker than a land tornado.
  • Clouds: cirrus (high, feathery), cumulus (cotton heaps), stratus (flat layers), nimbus (dark rain clouds).
  • Dew point: the temperature at which air becomes saturated and dew forms.
Local windWhere
LooHot, dry summer wind of north India (Punjab to Bihar)
Mango showersPre-monsoon showers in Kerala and Karnataka, help mangoes ripen
Cherry blossom (coffee) showersKarnataka
Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers)Evening storms in West Bengal and Assam; 'Bardoli Chheerha' in Assam
Chinook ('snow eater')Rockies, North America
FoehnAlps, Europe
SiroccoSahara to Italy
Harmattan ('the doctor')West Africa
MistralFrance (Rhone valley)

concepts.title: Oceans, straits and canals
concepts.body:
• Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean; Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep, about 11 km) is the deepest point. The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country.
  • Warm currents: Gulf Stream, Kuroshio. Cold currents: Labrador, Humboldt (Peru), Benguela, Canaries, California, Oyashio.
  • Spring tides (high) come at new and full moon; neap tides at the quarter moons.
  • 1 nautical mile = 1.852 km.
StraitJoins or separates

MalaccaMalay Peninsula and Sumatra

Bab-el-MandebYemen and Djibouti (Red Sea to Gulf of Aden)
GibraltarSpain and Morocco
BosphorusBlack Sea to Sea of Marmara (Istanbul)

BeringRussia and Alaska
BassAustralia and Tasmania

Nine Degree ChannelLakshadweep islands and Minicoy

Canals: Suez (Mediterranean to Red Sea, Egypt, 1869); Panama (Atlantic to Pacific, 1914); Kiel (North Sea to Baltic, Germany).

Grasslands: Prairies (North America), Pampas (Argentina), Steppes (Eurasia), Veld (South Africa), Downs (Australia), Llanos (Venezuela and Colombia), Savanna (Africa).

Köppen climate letters: A tropical, B dry, C warm temperate, D cold, E polar. In B climates, 'h' means hot and 'k' means cold, so a mid-latitude (cold) desert is BWk. Citrus fruits grow best in Mediterranean climates (dry summers, rainy winters).

The Indus is Pakistan's longest river; it rises in Tibet near Lake Manasarovar. Karachi is Pakistan's busiest seaport. Colombo is Sri Lanka's largest city.

concepts.title: India: location, extent and borders
concepts.body:
• Latitude about 8°4′N to 37°6′N; longitude about 68°7′E to 97°25′E. Area 3.287 million sq km: the 7th largest country, about 2.4% of world land.
  • The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.
  • Southernmost point: Indira Point (Great Nicobar). Mainland tip: Kanyakumari.
  • Largest state by area: Rajasthan; smallest: Goa. Most populous: Uttar Pradesh. Gujarat has the longest coastline among states.
  • Delhi borders only Haryana and Uttar Pradesh.
NeighbourIndian states and UTs on the border
Bangladesh (longest border)West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
ChinaLadakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh

MyanmarArunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram
PakistanGujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh

Border lines: Radcliffe Line (India with Pakistan and Bangladesh), McMahon Line (India and China in the east), Durand Line (Pakistan and Afghanistan).

concepts.title: Relief: Himalayas, peaks, passes, plateaus, islands
concepts.body:
• Three Himalayan ranges: Himadri (Greater, highest peaks), Himachal (Lesser, hill stations), Shiwalik (outer, with flat valleys called duns such as Dehradun).
  • Peaks: K2 (Godwin Austen, 8,611 m) is in the Karakoram; Kanchenjunga (8,586 m, Sikkim) is the highest peak on India's border; Nanda Devi is the highest wholly inside India; Anamudi (Kerala) is the highest in south India; Guru Shikhar (Mount Abu) is the highest in the Aravallis; Dhupgarh (Pachmarhi) in the Satpuras; Kalsubai is the highest in Maharashtra; Doddabetta is in the Nilgiris.
  • Plateaus: Deccan (lava, black soil), Chota Nagpur (minerals), Malwa, Meghalaya (Garo, Khasi, Jaintia hills).
  • Coasts: west coast (Konkan, Kanara, Malabar) is narrow; east coast (Northern Circars, Coromandel) is wide with deltas.
  • Islands: Andaman and Nicobar (Bay of Bengal, volcanic and hilly); Lakshadweep (coral, Arabian Sea, capital Kavaratti). Majuli on the Brahmaputra (Assam) is a large river island.
  • Gandikota gorge on the Pennar (Andhra Pradesh) is called the 'Grand Canyon of India'.
PassLocation and link

Five prayags on the Alaknanda (upstream to downstream): Vishnuprayag (Dhauliganga), Nandprayag (Nandakini), Karnaprayag (Pindar), Rudraprayag (Mandakini), Devprayag (Bhagirathi). West-flowing rivers into the Arabian Sea: Narmada, Tapi, Sabarmati, Mahi, Periyar. Most other peninsular rivers flow east into the Bay of Bengal and form deltas.

Treaties: Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, 19 September 1960 (World Bank brokered; eastern rivers Ravi, Beas, Sutlej to India; western rivers Indus, Jhelum, Chenab mostly to Pakistan). Ganga Water Treaty with Bangladesh, 1996. Mahakali Treaty with Nepal, 1996.

concepts.title: Climate and monsoon
concepts.body:
• India has a tropical monsoon climate. IMD seasons: winter (January to February), summer (March to May), south-west monsoon (June to September), post-monsoon or retreating monsoon (October to December).
  • The south-west monsoon reaches Kerala around 1 June and splits into an Arabian Sea branch and a Bay of Bengal branch.
  • Wettest places: Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Meghalaya). Driest areas: western Rajasthan (Jaisalmer) and Leh.
  • Western disturbances from the Mediterranean bring winter rain to Punjab and Haryana, which helps wheat (rabi).
  • Tamil Nadu gets most of its rain from the north-east (retreating) monsoon in October to December.
  • Rain-shadow: the leeward (east) side of the Western Ghats gets little rain.
  • El Niño (warm Pacific waters) usually weakens the Indian monsoon; La Niña usually strengthens it.
  • ITCZ: Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone, a low-pressure belt near the equator that shifts north in summer and pulls in the monsoon.
  • Coastal places have the least difference between summer and winter temperatures (maritime climate); inland places like Delhi have extreme (continental) climate.

concepts.title: Soils, crops and irrigation
concepts.body:
SoilWhere and whyGood for
Alluvial (most widespread)Northern plains and deltas; khadar is new, bhangar is old alluvium; rich in potashRice, wheat, sugarcane
Black (regur)Deccan lava plateau; holds moisture; rich in lime, iron, magnesiumCotton
RedOld crystalline rocks; red from iron oxide; Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, OdishaMillets, pulses
LateriteHeavy rain washes out nutrients (leaching); Kerala, Karnataka, hillsTea, coffee, cashew
Arid (desert)Rajasthan; sandy and salineBajra after irrigation
Peaty, marshyKerala, Sundarbans; rich in organic matterRice
SeasonSown and harvestedCrops
KharifJune to July, harvested September to OctoberRice, maize, jowar, bajra, cotton, jute, groundnut, soybean, arhar
RabiOctober to December, harvested March to AprilWheat, barley, gram, mustard, peas
ZaidMarch to June (summer)Watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, fodder
  • Shifting (slash and burn) cultivation: Jhum in the north-east; Podu in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha; Bewar in Madhya Pradesh.
  • Leading states (they can change by year): wheat and sugarcane, Uttar Pradesh; tea, Assam; coffee, Karnataka; rubber, Kerala; jute, West Bengal.
  • India is the largest producer of milk and pulses. China is the largest producer of rice and wheat; India is second.
  • Canals carry water by gravity. The Indira Gandhi Canal (Rajasthan) starts at Harike barrage. Tanks are common in south India; tube wells in the northern plains.

Steel plants: TISCO Jamshedpur (1907, private); Bhilai (Chhattisgarh, Soviet help); Rourkela (Odisha, German help); Durgapur (West Bengal, British help); Bokaro (Jharkhand, Soviet help); Visakhapatnam (shore-based).

Railways: first passenger train on 16 April 1853, Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane, about 34 km. Zone headquarters: Northern (New Delhi), Western (Mumbai Churchgate), Central (Mumbai CSMT), Southern (Chennai), Eastern (Kolkata), South Central (Secunderabad), Northeast Frontier (Maligaon, Guwahati), North Eastern (Gorakhpur), East Central (Hajipur), North Western (Jaipur), West Central (Jabalpur), North Central (Prayagraj), East Coast (Bhubaneswar), South Western (Hubballi), South East Central (Bilaspur).

Ports: Deendayal (Kandla, Gujarat, tidal port); Mumbai (natural harbour); Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva, biggest container port); Mormugao (Goa, iron ore); Kochi; V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin); Chennai; Kamarajar (Ennore); Visakhapatnam (deepest landlocked harbour); Paradip (Odisha); Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port (Kolkata, a river port). Roads: NH 44 (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) is the longest national highway; the Golden Quadrilateral links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata.

concepts.title: Population: Census 2011
concepts.body:
Census 2011 was the 15th census (7th after independence). The first synchronous census was in 1881; 1921 is the 'year of great divide' (the only decade when population fell). The next census, the first since 2011, uses 1 March 2027 as its reference date.

The gap between male and female literacy was the highest in Rajasthan.

varieties.name: Solar system and the Earth
varieties.how: Learn one tag per planet (smallest, hottest, largest, rings) and the four key dates. For time, use 15° = 1 hour.

example.q: Two places are 45° of longitude apart. What is the time difference?

varieties.name: Earth's interior, rocks and landforms
varieties.how: Sort rocks by origin (magma, layers, heat and pressure) and remember the 'from' pairs (marble from limestone). Link theories to scientists.

example.q: Marble is formed from which rock?
steps: It forms when limestone is changed by heat and pressure.

varieties.name: Atmosphere, winds and oceans
varieties.how: Learn layer order from the ground up (T, S, M, T, E) with one feature each. Learn local winds with the region.

example.q: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer found?
steps: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere, above it.

varieties.name: World geography
varieties.how: Learn record holders, city and river pairs, and straits with the two lands they separate.

example.q: Which strait separates Java and Sumatra?
steps: Malacca is between Malaysia and Sumatra.
Sunda Strait lies between Java (east) and Sumatra (west).

varieties.name: India: location and relief
varieties.how: Learn the 8 Tropic of Cancer states, the neighbours' border states, and passes by state from west (Zoji La) to east (Bom Di La).

example.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which state: Rajasthan, Odisha, Tripura, Jharkhand?
steps: Tropic of Cancer states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram.
Odisha is not in the list.

varieties.name: Rivers, dams, lakes and waterfalls
varieties.how: For each river know source, direction, main tributaries and the dam on it. Ask 'east or west flowing?' for peninsular rivers.

example.q: The Bhakra Nangal dam is on which river?
steps: Bhakra Nangal is in Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.
It is built on the Sutlej; its reservoir is Gobind Sagar.

varieties.name: Indian climate and monsoon
varieties.how: Learn the season months, which wind gives rain where, and the names of local winds and showers.

example.q: What are the hot, dry winds that blow over north India in May and June called?
steps: Pre-monsoon winds in north India are hot and dry.

varieties.name: Soils, crops and irrigation
varieties.how: Pair soil with its crop and region; pair crops with season (kharif monsoon, rabi winter, zaid summer).

example.q: Black soil is also known as:
steps: Black soil forms from Deccan lava and suits cotton.

varieties.name: Minerals, industry and transport
varieties.how: Learn mineral, state and the famous mine name together. For steel plants, remember the foreign partner.

example.q: Khetri is famous for which mineral?
steps: It is a major copper mining belt.

varieties.name: Population and census
varieties.how: Learn India's 2011 figures and the top and bottom state for each measure. Kerala tops sex ratio and literacy; Bihar tops density but is last in literacy.

example.q: According to Census 2011, which state had the lowest sex ratio?
steps: Kerala was highest (1084); Haryana was lowest (879).

tips: Planet order: 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles' (Mercury to Neptune).
Tropic of Cancer states west to east: 'Gu-Ra-M-Ch-J-W-T-M' (Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram).
Five prayags downstream: 'Vishnu Nand Karna Rudra Dev' (Vishnu, Nand, Karna, Rudra, Devprayag).
Atmosphere layers upward: 'The Smart Mice Talk Eagerly' (troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, exosphere).
Indus Treaty split: India gets the eastern three (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), Pakistan the western three (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab).
Census 2011 anchors: 943 sex ratio, 74% literacy, 382 density, 17.7% growth.
Sorrows: Kosi of Bihar, Damodar of Bengal, Brahmaputra of Assam, Hwang Ho of China.
traps: Narmada and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea; Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri flow east.
Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag, not Rudraprayag (Alaknanda and Mandakini).
Chilika is a brackish lagoon; Wular is the largest freshwater lake; Sambhar is a salt lake.
Venus, not Mercury, is the hottest planet, even though Mercury is nearer the Sun.
Kanchenjunga is the highest peak on India's border, but Nanda Devi is the highest wholly within India; K2 lies in the Karakoram.

questions.q: The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on which river?
questions.solution:
Bhakra Nangal Dam is on the Sutlej river (Himachal Pradesh–Punjab).
Memory hook: Two Punjab dams, two rivers: Bhakra on Sutlej, Pong on Beas.

questions.q: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.solution:
The Nile (Africa) is generally taken as the longest river in the world; the Amazon carries the most water.
Memory hook: Nile = Length, Amazon = Amount of water.

questions.q: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer found?
questions.solution:
The ozone layer lies in the stratosphere and absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays.
Memory hook: Stratosphere Shields us from UV.

questions.q: Which of these rivers flows westward into the Arabian Sea?
questions.solution:
Tapi and Narmada flow west through rift valleys into the Arabian Sea. Godavari, Krishna and Mahanadi flow east into the Bay of Bengal.
Memory hook: N–T go West (Narmada, Tapi).

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which state?
questions.solution:
The Tropic of Cancer passes through Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. Odisha lies south of it.
Memory hook: The line jumps from Jharkhand to West Bengal — Odisha is left below.

questions.q: Black soil is also known as:
questions.solution:
Black soil is called regur (or black cotton soil). It holds moisture and suits cotton. Bhangar and Khadar are old and new alluvium.
Memory hook: Regur — 'Real cotton grower'.

questions.q: At which place do the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet to form the Ganga?
questions.solution:
The Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet at Devprayag (Uttarakhand); from here the river is called the Ganga.
Memory hook: The holy river is born at the 'Dev' (god) prayag.

questions.q: The Indian Standard Time meridian (82°30′E) is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time by:
questions.solution:
Earth turns 1° in 4 minutes. 82.5° × 4 min = 330 min = 5 h 30 min.
Memory hook: 82.5 × 4 = 330 minutes.
